messages:
Jordan: Quick sync — we need a concrete playbook for migrating internal clients from our REST endpoints to gRPC/protobuf. Lots of teams are asking and we keep repeating the same advice.
Maya: +1. Can we include recommended gateway pattern, backwards-compat rules, and telemetry/quotas implications? :+1:
Kevin: Suggestion: start with a compatibility shim at the gateway that translates JSON -> proto for new clients and flags callers. Keeps service surface stable.
Jordan: Yeah. Gateway shim is non-invasive. But we need clear signals so platform can route by client capability (rest vs grpc) for canaries.
Sara: UX ask for Console: show per-client "transport" metric (rest|grpc) and a small drift chart. Ops should be able to filter by transport when troubleshooting.
Luc: For quotas, we must map units consistently. REST currently charges per-token as seen by API; gRPC streaming changes how tokens are reported. Need canonical token accounting at the gateway.
Anya: Can we standardize headers for capability negotiation? e.g. `x-rw-transport: grpc` and `x-rw-client-version: 1.2.0` so routing + telemetry is easy to attribute.
Kevin: +1 to headers. Also recommend `x-rw-proto-compat: stable|legacy|compat-v2` to indicate protobuf expectations.
Maya: For schema evolution, we should publish a tiny compatibility guide: avoid required fields, prefer reserved field numbers, and use explicit feature flags when changing semantics. Add a sample proto snippet in the playbook.
Jordan: Example proto vs JSON snippet for docs:
```
// proto
message GenerateRequest {
  string prompt = 1;
  int32 max_tokens = 2; // optional in later versions
}
// equivalent REST body
{
  "prompt": "hello",
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```
Maya: Love the snippet. Also include migration checklist: 1) add headers, 2) enable gateway shim, 3) rollout canary to 5% grpc-first clients, 4) validate telemetry and quotas, 5) promote.
Luc: Telemetry details: ensure we emit `transport`, `client_version`, `proto_schema_version`, `route_policy` as tags on traces and metrics. This prevents blind spots when we compare latencies.
Sara: Console: can we add a quick action to force-fallback to REST per-client if grpc fails? Ops will love that.
Kevin: Implement fallback as a routing policy in the gateway. Policy config example:
```
policy {
  name: "transport-preference"
  match: { header: "x-rw-transport", value: "grpc" }
  primary: grpc-cluster
  fallback: rest-cluster
  failover_threshold_ms: 300
}
```
Anya: How about rollout signals? We should define success SLOs: latency (p50/p95), error rate, and token accounting variance (<2%). If any exceed, auto rollback.
Jordan: Agree. Add a standard canary dashboard template in the playbook with panels for those metrics + per-transport breakdown.
Maya: Also call out the developer-facing contract: clients should accept `application/grpc+proto` and still support `application/json` for a transition window.
Luc: Ops note: gateway must normalize quota lookups so both transport types hit the same quota keys. We should detail implementation pitfalls (double counting on streaming reconnects).
Kevin: Testing: add an integration test harness that spins up the gateway shim and runs p50/p95 capture with both transports under synthetic load. Include script example in repo.
Sara: Can we put a short section in the playbook about observability cost? more metrics per-request adds cost; suggest sampling for traces but not counters.
Anya: Security: ensure mutual TLS still enforced for grpc and that gateway doesn't leak proto schema details in error messages.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for `transport-playbook` docs (build 2025.03.12-8) :rocket:
Jordan: Next steps: Maya + Kevin draft the playbook doc + example configs, Luc to write telemetry tagging conventions, Sara to sketch console panels. We'll sync next Tue 11a.
Maya: I'll make a PR with the initial playbook and a checklist.
Kevin: I'll add the gateway policy schema and the sample integration test.
Luc: I'll stub the telemetry naming RFC and share.
Sara: I'll mockup the console panels and add to the PR.
Anya: I'll review the security bits once draft is up.
Jordan: Thanks everyone. If you want, tag me in the PR and I'll shepherd the canary plan. :eyes:
